body:
# the contributor independent audits of the recovered slab and local scalar results


audit for OC. Each source was read in full against its displayed proofs.

## A. Exact slab first variation and genuine critical counterexamples

Source: `candidate 09cd5673b7dfb72e`.

The exact verifier was independently rerun: PASS3203 rational checks.

The product diamond has exactly four positive integer fibers, total
area8 and raw maximum3. The lower bound treats every oblique cap by
pairing opposite thresholds on centrally symmetric fibers, and treats
pure integer closed caps with their full boundary fiber. The five
displayed mass3 caps cover the whole mixed source and certify the upper
bound. Both actual contacts and every claimed critical cap are valid.

The residual's vertical sections give D_t+epsilon E=D_(t-epsilon),
not merely inclusion. Independently integrating the three cap traces
gives all three displayed area polynomials. Their minimum is indeed
the third trace in both stated parameter ranges. The derivatives
distinguish F from F-V: at L=1/2,t=1/4 the surplus derivative is
-11/16; at L=10,t=1/40 the credit derivative is-1979/160 and surplus
derivative-2299/160. The triple-core triangles and their containment
ranges are also correct. All are above OC, and the large-tilt example
does not claim to defeat an optimized-critical-menu premise.

The general first-variation proof correctly differentiates finite
maxima/minima through their active sets, then the positive part,
then the moving integration endpoints. All velocities are bounded,
giving dominated convergence. Compact convex planar section endpoints
are continuous even at projection endpoints: convex interpolation and
the appropriate semicontinuity give the two inequalities. Thus the
endpoint strip terms are justified, including interval birth at one
point and initially zero-area sections. The isolated lower-edge and
upper-edge special-case formulas require a positive-length section;
the source now states this and gives the correct collapsed-section
formula separately. General formula(10) already handled it correctly.

## B. Sharp two-sided scalar frontier at whole-body BM equality

Source: `candidate 8426c7487ce19740`.


When all corresponding closed endpoint sections are nonempty, their
weighted Minkowski sum is genuinely available, including tangent
zero-volume faces. BM gives the stated captured and residual root
bounds. If an opposite section is empty, its positive support gap
puts the full-dimensional residual sum strictly away from the cutting
plane. A proper target cut leaves a positive strip outside that sum,
which proves the excluded endpoint. This is a strict geometric
argument and does not treat an empty set as a zero-volume summand.

The unit-volume frusta have strictly increasing continuous prefix
CDFs with continuous quantiles, including0 and1. Their common-shape
homotheties and explicit translations realize the prescribed fractions
with one fixed halfspace and exact whole-body BM equality. At the two
cone limits they attain the two scalar endpoints. IVT suffices to fill
the interval; no unproved monotonicity of the interpolation is used.
Moving exactly the prescribed zero/one quantiles outside their support
realizes every remaining status case and the stated open endpoints.
The separate d=1 interval proof and the rational-weight integer-base
realization are correct. Extra integer fibers in the latter are
explicitly not claimed to have controlled depths.

The new affine interval source with lengths(1,3/2,2) is an actual
complete three-fiber body, has strict noheavy, and raw maximum7/4
at its unique middle midpoint. All critical caps have residuals
(0,3/4,2). The natural cap-cover program has optimum9/4; every
primal/KKT choice yields the same uniform terminal row, with gap1/6.
Whole-body BM is now tight in that very row, and the source own cap
is an exact gamma_1 half. This strengthens the earlier counter without
claiming a d>=2 globally critical realization or an OC failure.

The arbitrary-dimension opposite-status simplex construction has the
stated residual gap and can keep that gap positive while its fully
captured endpoint volume tends to zero. Its scope remains local.

## C. Separating the middle and pair directional infima loses the target

Source: `candidate 31c5f4602b138303`.


The actual source(epsilon T,T,T) has the asserted fibers and strict
noheavy. Its exact endpoint-only depth vanishes outside and on the
boundary of((1+epsilon)/2)T; strict separation or support-face cuts
give one shared ambient halfspace and preserve closed-boundary nullity.
Inside that section, own depth plus pair depth is bounded by5V/16.
Outside, pair depth is zero. The simplex centroid lies outside and
attains own depth Gamma_d V, so the exact optimized separated bound
is Gamma_d V for all d>=2. It is strictly below the required source
target by Gamma_d epsilon^d V/2.

The planar fractions and the optional safe-depth check against the
already audited tiny-endpoint theorem are correct. Formula(6) retains
the SAME continuous normal in the middle contribution and the
endpoint infimum; it separately includes both pure-integer caps.
That noncommutation is precisely the scope of this obstruction.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
